facts.text: The user is working on a topology problem about a topological space X and open sets A and B.
The user is trying to prove that the exterior of (A∪B) equals the intersection of the exteriors of A and B.
The user is using the notation S^e to mean the exterior of a set S.
The user is considering a point x being in the complement of the interior of A∪B.
The user believes that there exists an open set U ⊆ X with x ∈ U and U ⊆ X \ A.
The user corrects that there exists an open set U ⊆ X with x ∈ U and U ⊆ X \ (A∪B).
The user is considering the case x ∈ A^e ∩ B^e.
The user states that if x ∈ A^e ∩ B^e, then there are open sets U and V with x ∈ U and x ∈ V, with U ⊆ A^c and V ⊆ B^c.
The user defines W ⊆ A^c ∩ B^c and asks whether it is the same as (A∪B)^c.
The user states that since W is open, there exists an open set with x ∈ W and W ⊆ (A∪B)^c.
The user concludes that x ∈ (A∪B)^e by the definition of the exterior.
The user has a second problem about equipping R with the topology generated by the metric d(x,y)=|x−y|.
The user asks to compute the interior, exterior, and boundary of Q ⊆ R.
The user requests to use text format without LaTeX for the second problem.
